title: Holi, festival of colors
hookLine: the Hindu spring festival of colors; it begins the night before with Holika's bonfire and Prahlad walking out of the fire
tomorrow: on Eid, a man tried to stop girls singing. what did the Prophet say?

lines: A KING WHO WANTS TO BE WORSHIPPED.
cards: Holi morning can look like a paint factory burst open: powder in the air, everyone pink and green, strangers laughing. But Holi begins the night before, around a fire, with a story.
A demon king, Hiranyakashipu, demands that everyone worship him. His own son, Prahlad, won't. The boy keeps praying to Vishnu.
The king tries everything to kill him, and fails. Then the king's sister, Holika, offers a plan: she'll sit in a bonfire with the boy on her lap.

teach.h: PRAHLAD WALKS OUT OF THE FIRE.
teach.b: In the telling families share at the fire, Holika can't be burned. But the fire turns the other way. Holika burns, and Prahlad walks out unharmed, still saying Vishnu's name.
Prahlad's story is told in the Bhagavata Purana; the part with Holika is the one told at the bonfire.

This is why Holi begins with Holika Dahan, the burning of Holika: a bonfire the night before, where many Hindus remember that devotion outlasted cruelty, and that good outlasts evil even when evil holds the power.

teach.h: KRISHNA AND RADHA PLAY WITH COLOR.
teach.b: The colors come the next morning, and they carry another story: Krishna, playing with Radha and the cowherd girls of Braj, throwing color. So Holi holds both, the fire that clears and the play that follows.
And the colors aren't only fun.
For a morning, the powder covers everyone the same, old and young, and the usual lines between people loosen.
Some Hindus say that on Holi, old quarrels get forgiven too. The fire comes first; the color says the night is over.

how: On the night before Holi, Hindu communities light the Holika Dahan bonfire and retell Prahlad's story; the next morning people throw colored powder and water, share sweets and visit friends and family.

games.why: Holi begins with Holika Dahan, remembering how Prahlad's devotion outlasted the king's cruelty. the colors come the next morning.

practice: If you can, put on something bright right now, or hold anything colorful within reach. Look at the color for a moment and let your eyes rest in it.
Then close your eyes and think of one quarrel you'd be glad to see covered in color.
